title: Microbench playbook - prompt/quant experiments
content:
Purpose: quick running log + checklist for small-batch evals. Use this as an ephemeral notepad when I'm iterating on prompt variants and quant configs. Keep short notes, obs, and next steps.

---

TODAY'S GOALS:
- Validate 4-bit quantized 13B (q4f) end-to-end throughput on n2-standard-gpu cluster. Target median 95ms per token for seq_len=256 under batching=4.
- Sweep prompt priming patterns for hallucination regression in product FAQs.
- Capture two reproducible eval commands and baseline metrics.

RUNS (chronological):
1) run id: sofia-mb-0311-a (q4f, batch=4, fp16-kv cache disabled)
   - cmd: ./run_eval --model rdx-13b-q4f --seq 256 --batch 4 --cache off --seed 42
   - notes: first warmup slow, steady-state stable ~120ms/token; tail spikes when concurrency jumps. perplexity on dev-prompts: 17.8

2) run id: sofia-mb-0311-b (q4f, batch=4, cache=prefix)
   - cmd: ./run_eval --model rdx-13b-q4f --seq 256 --batch 4 --cache prefix --seed 42
   - notes: stable ~98ms/token, cache hit ratio ~0.32, small quality lift on follow-ups. hallucination spot-check: fewer false facts on FAQ prompts.

PROMPT BANK (short variants to test):
- P0: "You are an assistant. Answer concisely." + user question
- P1: "Answer with step-by-step reasoning and cite sources when available." + user question
- P2: "For a non-technical user, explain in plain language." + user question
- P3: "If uncertain, say 'I might be mistaken' and ask for clarification." + user question

QUANT NOTES / HYPOTHESES:
- q4f seems fine latency-wise but occasionally regresses on rare tokens (names/dates). hypothesis: mixed-precision path for softmax drops fidelity at extreme logits.
- Try q4f with per-channel clipping and temperature=0.94 in inference wrapper.
- If quality drop persists, re-run a smaller subset with q8h to compare memory/latency tradeoff.

METRICS TO CAPTURE (scripted):
- median_ms_per_token, p95_ms_per_token, cache_hit_rate, sample_perplexity, exact_match_FAQ, hallucination_rate_manual
- Make sure logs include "route_id", "alloc_id", and token-level timing.

OBSERVATIONS / QUICK IDEAS:
- When batch=1 latency is dominated by scheduling (45ms overhead). Check batching buffer timeout (currently 8ms). Lowering to 4ms might help p50 at the cost of throughput.
- Prompt P1 reduces hallucination but increases length of output -> token cost up ~18%. Tradeoff worth for high-value flows.

ACTION / TODO (next):
- [ ] Re-run sofia-mb-0311-b with per-channel clipping enabled (config: clip=0.015).
- [ ] Create a focused eval (50 examples) comparing q4f vs q8h on the FAQ prompt set (priority: reduce hallucination). Add to CI smoke tests if delta > 3% EM improvement.
- [ ] File a perf issue if p95 > 250ms under realistic concurrency (JIRA-AML-4823).
- [ ] Sync with Ethan next Tue about KV cache heuristics; share logs and flame graphs.
- [ ] Add the best prompt template to product-guidance draft (link to be added).

NOTES TO SELF:
- Keep seeds recorded. Avoid changing temperature between runs unless explicitly experimenting.
- Save output samples in /mnt/exp/sofia/0311/ with run_id metadata.

Loose ideas: test a mini A/B in console: have model return a short confidence token at end of answers (e.g., [CONF:0.82]) to help front-end decide need for human fallback. Quick hackable with post-process classifier.

End of file.
